Mr. Vice President, Grenada has already begun implementing several of the recommendations we have accepted, focusing on areas of urgent national priority. Human rights and climate change. Grenada recognizes that climate change is not only an environmental challenge, but also a human rights issue, threatening the right to life, health, housing, and livelihoods of our people. Grenada's updated national adaptation plan is a bold people-centered roadmap to climate resilience led by our national climate change committee and supported by the NAP global network through the International Institute for Sustainable Development. It harnesses improved data collection, stronger institutions, and inclusive engagement to protect coastlines, secure food, water, and energy systems, and safeguard health, education, and livelihood. The plan integrates gender and child-responsive approaches, adopts a human security lens, and addresses loss and damage, while aligning with the nationally determined contributions and sectoral adaptation plans. We extend sincere appreciation to the government of Germany for its general support in advancing this work. As Grenada enters 2025 to 2030 implementation phase of the NAP, the NAP will rally community voices, youth, gender advocates, and technical partners to mobilize the financing and collaboration needed to build a resilient, inclusive future for all Grenadians. Protection of vulnerable groups. Draft legislation is being finalized to strengthen protections for persons with disabilities and to fulfill Grenada's obligations under the Convention of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. The bill will require accessibility audits and the adoption of universal design standards for public buildings and transport. mandate reasonable accommodation across public services, and establish clear timelines and enforcement mechanisms. It will expand inclusive education through teacher training, curriculum adaptation, and provision of assistive technologies and learning support services. This bill also proposes a dedicated oversight mechanism and monitoring framework, backed by a targeted budget and capacity building for local authorities. It calls for sustained consultation and partnership with disability organizations to ensure implementation is effective, rights-based, and responsive to the needs of persons with disabilities. Grenada continues to advance gender equality through both legislative reform and international cooperation. Cabinet has recently approved the development of draft legislation on gender responsive care, which includes extended maternity leave, the introduction of parental leave, child benefits for low income families, and enhanced protections for domestic and care workers. These reforms are firmly aligned with Grenada's commitment under the Convention of the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women and the Beijing Platform for Action. In parallel, Grenada is working diligently with the Commonwealth Secretariat through its office here in Geneva to finalize a national CEDAW report, further strengthening our international reporting obligations. This collaborative process has enabled us to assess the recent policy initiatives, identify gaps, and reaffirm our commitment to transparency, accountability, and the full realization of women's rights in accordance with international law. Correctional reform. The issue of prison overcrowding and the need for enhanced rehabilitation services have been the subject of multiple recommendations. each underscoring the urgent necessity for structural reform and improved inmate outcomes. In response, the government has accepted these recommendations and have recently completed the design for a new correctional facility that will allow for both the reconstruction and expansion of the existing infrastructure. This modern facility estimated to cost US $50 million to construct and outfit is envisioned as a transformative space that prioritizes human conditions guided by the Nelson Mandela rules, rehabilitation and reintegration. Grenada therefore makes a sincere appeal at this forum for strategic partnership support, financial, technical, and programmatic in helping to realize this national critical objective, which stands to benefit not only the incarcerated population, but the society at large. National Human Rights Institution. Mr. Vice President, Grenada is renewing efforts to establish a national human rights institution working with partners such as the Commonwealth Secretariat through its Small States Office here in Geneva, to identify a model that fits our national context and fully complies with the Paris Principles. Mr. Vice President, even among recommendations not yet fully accepted, Grenada is taking concrete steps forward. The Status of Children Bill will eliminate discrimination based on birth status, ensuring equal rights for all children. The Marriage Amendment Bill raises the legal age of marriage to 18, protecting children from early and forced marriage in line with the Convention on the Rights of the Child. The Civil Legal Responsibility Bill seeks to amend the Age of Civil Legal Responsibility Act to vest minors aged 16 and over with the full legal capacity to consent independently to sexual and reproductive health treatments, including diagnostic procedures. Mr. President, a wide range of recommendations addressed economic social rights as fundamental pillars of human rights. These recommendations covered education, health, housing, and work. The State of Kuwait approached them in a positive spirit, affirming that sustainable development and protection rights are two sides of the same coin. In the field of education, we continue to provide free schooling to more than half a million students, including non-Kuwaitis, reflecting our commitment to equal opportunity and non-discrimination. Efforts are underway to modernize the curricula and upgrade school infrastructure. In the health sector, Kuwait has strengthened its comprehensive healthcare system through the expansion of primary health centers and specialized hospitals, as well as adopting national programs to combat chronic diseases and promote mental health.
